$comment: THE CANARY REGISTRY (M5.E8, FR3). Every instruction the adherence harness measures,
paired with the observable trace it should produce — declared BEFORE any run.
AC3.3 exists because a trace chosen after seeing the output is a rationalization, not a
prediction. Same reasoning applies to `verdictRule` below: the mapping from run counts to
a verdict is fixed here in advance, so nobody gets to pick a threshold after seeing 3/3
`deletions[]` names every site that ORDERS the instruction — each entry either a
`section` (deleted to the next same-or-higher heading) or a `line` (an exact substring).
Each anchor must occur EXACTLY ONCE in its real file: a target that has drifted out would
delete nothing, make both arms identical, and read as INERT. A test asserts that count
for every entry, not just the first.
Superseded `deleteSection`/`deleteLine` (M5.E15). Those held ONE anchor, so a canary whose
instruction was stated in five files still produced a one-file mutation and the 'deleted'
arm kept the instruction four more times — recorded as `B55`. The loader now REFUSES a
canary that declares neither key rather than falling back to one-file behavior.
Deliberately conservative. With N runs of a nondeterministic process, anything short of
a unanimous split is reported as INDETERMINATE rather than rounded into a finding.
INDETERMINATE is an honest answer; a 2-of-3 'obeyed' is not.
verdictRule.indeterminate: anything else, any failed run, or a backwards result
verdictRule.refuses: no verdict at all unless the mutation was proven to reach the agent

$isolationNote: DIRECTIVE scope (M5.E15, `D-M5E15-1`). The control arm deletes every site that ORDERS
the call, not every site that mentions the function. `B55` recorded the previous scope
as the defect: deleting only execute.md left plan/verify/review/ship still ordering the
same call, so the 'instruction-deleted' arm still carried the instruction four more
times. The re-run under that scope returned treatment 3/3, control 1/3 = INDETERMINATE.
ship.md is declared by LINE, not section, and the difference is load-bearing: its
`### 5. Update State` heading also orders `completePhase` and discusses `markFresh`.
A section delete there would remove instructions the experiment is not measuring —
over-deletion, which invalidates a verdict just as surely as under-deletion.
Both mentions of the function in ship.md sit on that one line, so the line delete
still leaves zero residue in the file.
Sites that TEACH the rule without ordering it (discuss.md, index.md, calibrate.md),
DOCUMENT the semantics (references/state-schema.md), or ARE the capability
(tools/lib/state.js) are deliberately NOT deleted. Stripping them would produce a
differently-invalid control: an agent that cannot read the schema is not the same
$deletionNote: SECTION-level, not line-level, and the difference decided a verdict.
The first control arm deleted only the imperative line. That left the section heading
('Phase entry — record the phase') plus two paragraphs naming `transitionPhase` and
explaining exactly when to call it — so the 'instruction-deleted' arm still contained the
instruction three more times. Its first live run produced the trace and would have been
recorded as INERT: 'M5.E9's fix does nothing.' It was not inert; the control was not a
control. A test now asserts the mutated file does not mention the function at all.

trace.expect: STATE.md `phase` advances to EXECUTE, and `completed_phases` grows by the phase being left

why: This is the instruction M5.E9 shipped and could not verify. It said so in its own test
header rather than let a passing test imply otherwise, and that admission is what opened
this Epic. Measuring it first is the honest choice: the harness's first subject is the
claim its own author flagged as unproven.
It is also a fair test rather than a rigged one. The rule was added to four command files
in the release immediately before this Epic, so there is no long history of agents having
been trained on it by repetition in this repo.
Named worst case, and it is an acceptable one: if this comes back INERT, Signal will have
spent an Epic proving one of its own shipped fixes does nothing. That is what a real
measurement is for. It is recorded here, before the run, so the result cannot later be
reframed as a harness defect and tuned away.
$rewordNote: M5.E13 S2.t4 (`B48`) reworded the measured instruction to be CONDITIONAL on
preconditions passing. That invalidates the OBEYED verdict M5.E8 recorded
against the previous wording — a verdict measures a specific text, not a topic.
The section anchor is unchanged because the section HEADING was deliberately left
alone; only the body moved. The control arm's guarantee (the mutated file must
not mention transitionPhase at all) still holds because every mention lives
